title: ANOVA & Comparing Multiple Groups
interviewAnswer: ANOVA tests whether group means differ more than expected from within-group variability under model assumptions. A significant omnibus test does not say which groups differ, so post-hoc comparisons require care.
keyPoints: Assumptions include independence and model-specific variance/error structure.
why: ANOVA & Comparing Multiple Groups appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: ANOVA tests whether group means differ more than expected from within-group variability under model assumptions. A significant omnibus test does not say which groups differ, so post-hoc comparisons require care. Assumptions include independence and model-specific variance/error structure. Post-hoc tests need multiplicity control. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Compare average processing time across four deployment configurations before pairwise follow-ups.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.

production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
